questions.q: In the Anthropic Messages API response, where does the model's reply text live?
options: Directly in a top-level "text" field
In content[0].text, since content is an array of blocks
In choices[0].message.content
In a field called "reply"
questions.explain: The response's content field is an array of content blocks; a text block has type "text" and a text field.

questions.q: Why does this course call the OpenAI-style shape 'OpenAI-style' rather than 'the standard'?
options: Because it's the only shape any AI provider uses
Because Anthropic invented it first
Because many other providers and tools (like vLLM and Ollama) imitate its response shape, but it isn't the only one
Because it has no real adoption outside OpenAI
questions.explain: OpenAI's Chat Completions shape is widely copied, but Anthropic's Messages API uses a genuinely different shape — there are at least two real families.

questions.q: In an OpenAI-style Chat Completions response, what does "finish_reason": "stop" correspond to in Anthropic's Messages API?
options: usage.output_tokens
content[0].type
model
stop_reason: "end_turn"
questions.explain: finish_reason and stop_reason both answer 'why did the model stop generating' — they're the equivalent field under different names.

questions.q: What does the Anthropic Messages API's usage.input_tokens field tell you?
options: How many tokens your prompt/messages consumed, which affects your bill
How many words were in the model's reply
The maximum tokens the model is allowed to generate
The model's version number
questions.explain: usage.input_tokens counts tokens consumed by what you sent in; usage.output_tokens counts what the model generated back.

questions.q: Why is the Anthropic Messages API's content field an array instead of a plain string?
options: Because JSON doesn't support strings
It's a historical accident with no current purpose
Because every response always contains exactly two blocks
So a single response can mix different block types, like text and tool calls
questions.explain: An array of content blocks lets one response carry multiple kinds of content (text, tool_use, etc.) — essential once Lesson 13 introduces tool calling.
